literature_unverified_here.note: NOTHING in this object was computed or reproduced in this project, and no number is quoted for it. Gas-phase hydroxide with a tertiary alkyl halide is a studied competition, but this file records only the QUALITATIVE expectation, because quoting a barrier from memory is worse than quoting nothing: it would be unfalsifiable and unattributable at once. If a number is wanted here later it has to arrive with a citation and, preferably, a calculation in docs/experiments/.
literature_unverified_here.qualitative_expectation: With a strong base and a tertiary substrate, elimination is expected to dominate substitution; back-side attack at a tertiary carbon is sterically hindered. In the gas phase, with no solvent to stabilise a carbocation, the stepwise ionisation route is expected to be far more costly than it is in polar protic solvent.
literature_unverified_here.status: PREDICTION this benchmark can falsify, not an input. Per ../README.md rule 5 no part of it appears in CRITERIA.md.

textbook_labels.claim: The textbook says tert-butyl chloride ionises (SN1/E1, stepwise, via a carbocation) rather than being attacked directly (SN2/E2, concerted).
textbook_labels.status: This is exactly the statement ../TAXONOMY.md refuses to put in the premise. A carbocation intermediate is a MECHANISTIC claim; on the potential-energy surface the only measurable question is whether the channel has a confirmed minimum between reactants and products. Both answers pass; failing to answer is the only failure.

what_this_grid_reports.substitution_channel: is there a confirm_minimum-passing minimum between the reactant complex and the substitution products
what_this_grid_reports.elimination_channel: the same question, independently, on the elimination channel
what_this_grid_reports.competition: both channels are reported from ONE run on ONE substrate, because they compete for it. Reporting them from two runs would turn the real question into two single-choice questions -- ../TAXONOMY.md B.
